en: Theravāda Vinayapiṭaka Cūḷavagga 22.
The Chapter on the Seven Hundred [Nuns] (Sattasatikakkhandhaka)
Now at that time, one hundred years after the Blessed One had attained final Nibbāna, the Vajjiputta monks of Vesālī were propounding ten practices in Vesālī:

"The practice of salt in a horn is allowable; the practice of the two-finger-breadth is allowable; the practice of the interval between villages is allowable; the practice of the monastery is allowable; the practice of subsequent consent is allowable;
the practice of what has been customary is allowable; the practice of unchurned milk is allowable; the practice of whey..."
"It is allowable to drink; it is allowable to have a sitting mat without a border; it is allowable to accept gold and silver.
Now at that time, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, while wandering on tour among the Vajjis, arrived at Vesālī.
There, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta dwelt at Vesālī in the Gabled Hall in the Great Wood.

Now at that time, on the Uposatha day, the Vajjiputtaka monks of Vesālī filled a bronze bowl with water, placed it in the midst of the Saṅgha of monks, and said to the Vesālī lay followers as they arrived:
“Give, friends, a kahāpaṇa coin, or half a coin, or a quarter, or even a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha;
there will be something for the Saṅgha to do with the requisites.”
When this was said, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta said this to the lay followers of Vesālī:
“Friends, do not give even a single kahāpaṇa, a half, a quarter, or a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha.
It is not allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans to accept gold and silver.”
The ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, do not consent to gold and silver;
the ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, do not accept gold and silver;
the ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, have laid aside gems and gold, and are free from gold and silver.

Even though they were being addressed in this way by the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, the lay followers of Vesālī still did not give even a single kahāpaṇa, half a kahāpaṇa, a quarter, or a māsaka coin to the Saṅgha.
Then, at the end of that night, the Vajjiputtaka bhikkhus of Vesālī set aside a share for the bhikkhu’s portion and divided that gold among themselves.
Thereupon, the Vajjiputtaka bhikkhus of Vesālī said this to the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta:
“This is your share of the gold, friend Yasa.
“I have no share of the gold, friend; I do not accept gold.
Then the Vajjiputta monks of Vesālī—
“Friends, this Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta reviles and abuses the faithful and confident lay followers, and causes them to lose confidence.
Come now, let us perform an act of reconciliation against him. So they performed an act of reconciliation against him.
Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta said this to the Vajjiputta monks of Vesālī:
“Friends, it has been prescribed by the Blessed One:
‘A messenger should be given to a monk who has had a procedure of reconciliation performed against him.
Friends, give me a monk as a messenger.”
Then the Vajjiputtaka bhikkhus of Vesālī, having appointed one bhikkhu, gave him as a companion messenger to the venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta.
Then the venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, together with that companion bhikkhu, entered Vesālī and said this to the lay followers of Vesālī:
"I am supposedly reviling, abusing, and causing lack of confidence in you, venerable lay followers, who are faithful and devoted."
I am one who says that what is non-Dhamma is non-Dhamma, that what is Dhamma is Dhamma, that what is non-discipline is non-discipline, and that what is discipline is discipline.
Friends, on one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There, friends, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
“Bhikkhus, there are these four defilements of the moon and the sun, by which defilements being defiled, the moon and the sun do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate.
What are the four? Cloud, bhikkhus, is a defilement of the moon and the sun, by which defilement being defiled, the moon and the sun do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate.”
"Monks, mist is an obscuration of the moon and sun, by which obscuration the moon and sun, being obscured, do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.
Smoke-dust, monks, is an obscuration of the moon and sun, by which obscuration the moon and sun, being obscured, do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate."
“Monks, Rāhu, the lord of the asuras, is an obscuration of the moon and sun; obscured by which obscuration, the moon and sun do not burn, do not shine, and do not radiate.
These, monks, are the four obscurations of the moon and sun; obscured by which obscurations, the moon and sun do not burn, do not shine, and do not radiate.”
"In the same way, monks, there are these four defilements of recluses and brahmins, by which some recluses and brahmins, being defiled, do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.
What are the four?
There are, monks, some recluses and brahmins who drink fermented liquor, they drink distilled spirits, and they do not abstain from drinking fermented and distilled liquors."
This, monks, is the first defilement of some ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.
Furthermore, monks, some ascetics and brahmins engage in sexual intercourse; they are not abstinent from sexual intercourse.
This, monks, is the second defilement of some ascetics and brahmins, by which defilement being defiled, some ascetics and brahmins do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.
Furthermore, monks, some recluses and brahmins accept gold and silver; they do not abstain from accepting gold and silver.
This, monks, is the third defilement of some recluses and brahmins, by which defilement they are defiled and do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.
Furthermore, monks, some recluses and brahmins maintain their lives by wrong livelihood.
“Not abstaining from wrong livelihood— this, monks,
is the fourth defilement of recluses and brahmins, by which defilement some recluses and brahmins are defiled and do not glow,

do not shine, and do not radiate. These, monks, are the four defilements of recluses and brahmins, by which defilements some recluses and brahmins are defiled and do not glow, do not shine, and do not radiate.”
This, friends, the Blessed One said.
Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:
“Defiled by lust and hatred, ...”
Some recluses and brahmins,
beings shrouded in ignorance,
delight in forms that are dear.
They drink liquor and fermented spirits,
they indulge in sexual intercourse,
and [they accept] silver and gold.
The ignorant consent to them;
some recluses and brahmins live by wrong livelihood.
These defilements have been declared by the Buddha,
the Kinsman of the Sun;
those who are defiled by these defilements—
Some ascetics and brahmins do not practice austerity, nor do they teach;
being impure and full of passion, they are like deer.
Enveloped by darkness,
slaves to craving with their snares,
they increase the terrible cemetery.
“They take up renewed existence.
It is for this reason, it seems, that I revile, abuse, and cause displeasure toward those venerable lay followers who are faithful and confident—
though I am one who says that what is non-Dhamma is non-Dhamma, that what is Dhamma is Dhamma, that what is non-discipline is non-discipline, and that what is discipline is discipline.
"Friends, on one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, while the royal assembly was sitting together and gathered in the royal palace, this discussion arose among them:
'Is it allowable for the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, to accept gold and silver?'"
"The ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, accept gold and silver;
the ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, receive gold and silver.
Now at that time, friends, the village headman Maṇicūḷaka was sitting in that assembly.
Then, friends, the village headman Maṇicūḷaka said this to that assembly:
“Sirs, do not speak thus.
It is not allowable for the ascetics, the sons of the Sakyan, to accept gold and silver.”
"Monks, followers of the Sakyan son, do not consent to gold and silver;
monks, followers of the Sakyan son, do not accept gold and silver;
monks, followers of the Sakyan son, have laid aside gems and gold, and are free from gold and silver."
"Friends, the village headman Maṇicūḷaka was indeed able to convince that assembly.
Then, friends, having convinced that assembly, the village headman Maṇicūḷaka approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, friends, the village headman Maṇicūḷaka said this to the Blessed One:"
“Here, venerable sir, while the king’s assembly was sitting together and gathered in the royal palace, this discussion arose:
‘Is it allowable for the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, to accept gold and silver?
Do the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, consent to gold and silver?’”
"The ascetics, followers of the Sakyan son, accept gold and silver.
When this was said, venerable sir, I said to that assembly:
"Noble ladies, do not speak thus."
Gold and silver are not permitted for the recluses, sons of the Sakyan;
the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, do not accept gold and silver;
the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, do not take hold of gold and silver.
"The ascetics, sons of the Sakyans, have laid aside jewels and gold; they are free from bullion and silver.
"I was indeed able, Bhante, to convince that assembly.
In answering thus, Bhante, am I one who speaks in accordance with what has been said by the Blessed One, and do I not misrepresent the Blessed One?"
‘I do not misrepresent him with what is false; I explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate criticism or rebuttal can find ground for reproach against me?
‘Truly, headman, in explaining it thus, you speak my words exactly as they were spoken.’”
You do not misrepresent me with what is untrue; you explain in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate criticism or reproach can be leveled against you.
For indeed, headman, it is not permissible for the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, to accept gold and silver;
the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, do not consent to gold and silver.
The ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, do not accept gold and silver;
the ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, have laid aside gems and gold and are free from gold and silver.
For that person, headman, for whom gold and silver are permissible, even the five strands of sensual pleasure are permissible.

"O village headman, you should categorically hold this: for one for whom the five strands of sensual pleasure are appropriate, it is the nature of a non-ascetic, the nature of one who is not a son of the Sakyan.
Moreover, O village headman, I say this: grass should be sought by one who needs grass."
Wood must be sought by one who needs wood;
a cart must be sought by one who needs a cart;
a person must be sought by one who needs a person.
"But, headman, I do not say that by any means whatsoever should gold and silver be accepted or sought after.
It is for saying this that I revile, abuse, and cause displeasure toward those venerable lay followers who are faithful and confident;
I, who call what is non-Dhamma "non-Dhamma," and what is Dhamma "Dhamma," and who call what is non-discipline "non-discipline," and what is discipline "discipline."
"Friends, on one occasion the Blessed One, concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan son at Rājagaha, prohibited gold and silver and laid down a training rule.
Yet I, speaking thus, reviled, abused, and caused displeasure to the venerable lay followers who were faithful and confident;
I said that what is non-Dhamma is non-Dhamma, that what is Dhamma is Dhamma, that what is non-discipline is non-discipline, and that what is discipline is discipline."
When this was said, the lay followers of Vesālī said to the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta:
“Venerable sir, the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta alone is a recluse, a son of the Sakyan;
all these others are not recluses, they are not sons of the Sakyan.”
“Venerable sir, let the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta dwell in Vesālī.
We shall exert ourselves on behalf of the noble Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta regarding the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick.
Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, having persuaded the lay followers of Vesālī, returned to the monastery together with a monk acting as his attendant.
Then the Vajjiputtaka bhikkhus of Vesālī asked the messenger bhikkhu:
"Friend, have the lay followers of Vesālī been made to apologize by Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta?
"Friends, an offense has been committed against us by the lay followers."
“Only the ascetic Kākaṇḍakaputta has been made a Sakyan-son;
we have all been made non-ascetics and non-Sakyan-sons.
Then the Vajjiputtaka bhikkhus of Vesālī—
“Friends, this Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta has announced himself to householders without being authorized by us;
come, let us carry out a formal act of suspension against him.
Desiring to carry out that formal act of suspension against him, they assembled.
Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, having risen up into the air, alighted at Kosambī.
Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta sent a messenger to the presence of the monks from Pāvā and the monks from Avantī and the Southern Route, saying:
"Let the Venerable Ones come; let them come."
We shall take up this legal issue.
Previously, non-Dhamma was being promoted and the Dhamma was being obstructed;
non-Vinaya was being promoted and the Vinaya was being obstructed.
“Those who speak what is contrary to the Dhamma become powerful, while those who speak according to the Dhamma become weak;
those who speak contrary to the Vinaya become powerful, while those who speak according to the Vinaya become weak.
Now at that time, the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī was dwelling on Mount Ahogaṅga.

Then the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta went to Mount Ahogaṅga, where the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī was staying. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī and sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta said this to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī:
"Venerable sir, these Vajjiputta monks from Vesālī are propounding ten points at Vesālī."

The practice of carrying salt in a horn is permitted; the practice of two-finger-breadth is permitted; the practice of traveling between villages is permitted; the practice of staying within one’s own monastery is permitted;
the practice of subsequent consent is permitted; the practice of customary behavior is permitted; the practice of consuming curdled milk is permitted; it is permitted to drink whey;
it is permitted to have a sitting mat without a fringe; it is permitted to accept gold and silver.
"Come now, venerable sir, we shall take up this legal issue.
Previously, what was non-Dhamma shone forth while the Dhamma was suppressed;
what was non-Vinaya shone forth while the Vinaya was suppressed."
“Those who speak what is contrary to the Dhamma become powerful, while those who speak according to the Dhamma become weak;
those who speak what is contrary to the Vinaya become powerful, while those who speak according to the Vinaya become weak.
“It is so, friend,” the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī replied to the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta.
Then about sixty bhikkhus from Pāvā—
all of whom were forest-dwellers, all alms-collectors, all wearers of rag-robes, all possessors of the three robes, and all Arahants—
assembled on Mount Ahogaṅga.
About eighty monks from Avantī and the Southern Region—
some of whom were forest-dwellers, some alms-collectors, some wearers of rag-robes, and some who owned only three robes— all of whom were arahants,
assembled on Mount Ahogaṅga.
Then, as the elder bhikkhus were deliberating, it occurred to them:
"This legal issue is indeed harsh and violent; which faction might we obtain so that we may be stronger in this legal issue?"
Now at that time, the Venerable Revata was staying at Soreyya—
he who was learned, a master of the tradition, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikā, wise, competent, intelligent, modest, scrupulous, and desirous of training.
Then it occurred to those elder bhikkhus:
“This Venerable Revata is residing at Soreyya— he is learned, of inherited knowledge,
a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Matikas, wise, competent, intelligent, modest, scrupulous, and desirous of training.
If we can gain the support of the Venerable Revata, then we shall be much stronger in this legal matter.”
The Venerable Revata heard with his purified divine ear-element, which surpasses that of humans,
the elder bhikkhus as they were deliberating.
Upon hearing this, it occurred to him:
"This legal issue is indeed harsh and violent.
It would not be fitting for me to withdraw from such a legal issue."
"Now these monks will be arriving.
Being crowded by them, I shall not go with ease.
What if I were to depart beforehand?"
Then the Venerable Revata went from Soreyya to Saṅkassa.
When the elder bhikkhus had gone to Soreyya, they asked:
"Where is the Venerable Revata?"
They said this to him:
"Venerable Revata has gone to Saṅkassa.
Then the Venerable Revata went from Saṅkassa to Kaṇṇakujja.
Then the elder bhikkhus went to Saṅkassa and asked,
"Where is the venerable Revata?
They replied thus:
“Venerable Revata has gone to Kaṇṇakujja.
Then the Venerable Revata went from Kaṇṇakujja to Udumbara.
After the elder monks had gone to Kaṇṇakujja, they asked:
“Where is the Venerable Revata?
They replied,
“The Venerable Revata has gone to Udumbara.”
Then the Venerable Revata went from Udumbara to Aggaḷapura.
When the elder monks arrived at Udumbara, they asked,
"Where is the Venerable Revata?"
They said this to him:
"Venerable Revata has gone to Aggaḷapura.
Then the venerable Revata went from Aggaḷapura to Sahajāti.
Then the elder monks, having gone to Aggaḷapura, asked,
"Where is the Venerable Revata?
They replied as follows:
“Venerable Revata has gone to Sahajāti.
Then the elder bhikkhus sought out the venerable Revata at Sahajāti.
Then the venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī said this to the venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta:

“Friends, this venerable Revata is learned, one who has mastered the tradition, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikā; he is wise, competent, intelligent, modest, scrupulous, and desirous of training.
If we were to question the venerable Revata on a matter, he would be capable of spending the entire night with a single question alone.
Furthermore, the venerable Revata will now request his pupil, the reciter-monk Sarabhaṅga.”
"Therefore, at the conclusion of that bhikkhu’s recitation, you should approach the Venerable Revata and ask him about these ten points.
"Yes, venerable sir," the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta replied to the Venerable Sambhūta Sāṇavāsī.
Then the Venerable Revata requested his pupil, the bhikkhu who was the reciter.

Then, at the conclusion of that monk’s recitation, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta approached the Venerable Revata; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Revata, he sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta said this to the Venerable Revata:
“Venerable sir, is the practice of the salt-in-a-horn permissible?”
“Friend, what is this ‘practice of the salt-horn’?
“It is allowable, venerable sir, to carry salt in a horn with the thought:
‘Wherever there is no salt, there I shall consume it.’”
“It is not allowable, friend.
“Is the two-finger-breadth allowance allowable, Bhante?
“What is this two-finger-breadth allowance, friend?”
“Venerable sir, is it permissible to eat food at an improper time when two finger-breadths of shadow have passed?
“It is not permissible, friend.
“Venerable sir, is the ‘village-interval’ practice permissible?”
“Friend, what is this ‘allowance for traveling between villages’?
“It is allowable, venerable sir, for one who has finished eating and refused further food to eat food that is not left over, thinking: ‘Now I shall go to another village.
“Friend, it is not allowable.”
“Venerable sir, is the ‘practice of the same residence’ allowable?
“What is this ‘practice of the same residence,’ friend?
“Venerable sir, is it allowable for several residences that share the same boundary to perform the Uposatha separately?”
“It is not allowable, friend.
“Is it allowable, Bhante, by way of approval?
“What is that, friend, which is ‘allowable by way of approval’?”
“Venerable sir, is it permissible for a Saṅgha that is incomplete to perform an official act [with the thought],
‘We shall grant formal consent when the monks who have arrived have come’?
“It is not permissible, friend.”
“Venerable sir, is the ‘practice of what has been habitually done’ allowable?
“What is this, friend, that is called the ‘practice of what has been habitually done’?
“Venerable sir, it is allowable for me to practice that which was habitually practiced by my preceptor, and that which was habitually practiced by my teacher.”
“Friend, some established practices are allowable, while others are not.
“Venerable sir, is the practice of consuming unchurned milk-curd allowable?
“Friend, what is this practice of consuming unchurned milk-curd?”

“Venerable sir, is it allowable for one who has finished his meal and refused further food to drink that milk which has lost its state as milk but has not yet reached the state of curd, provided it is not left over? “It is not allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink whey? “It is not allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hoof-print? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a puddle? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a cow’s footprint? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a horse’s footprint? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a donkey’s footprint? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a camel’s footprint? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a well? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a pond? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a lake? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a pool? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a stream? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a river? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from the ocean? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a rain cloud? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a cistern? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a trough? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a bucket? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a jar? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a pot? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a bowl? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a cup? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a conch shell? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a coconut shell? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a gourd? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out tree trunk? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a bamboo joint? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out horn? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out skull? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out leather bag? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out hide? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out cloth? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out mat? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out basket? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out wooden vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out stone? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out brick? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out tile? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out metal vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out bell-metal vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out copper vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out iron vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out bronze vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out glass vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out crystal vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out pearl vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out gem vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out coral vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out amber vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out lapis lazuli vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out ruby vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out sapphire vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out diamond vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out emerald vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out topaz vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out cat’s-eye vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out moonstone vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out sunstone vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out quartz vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out agate vessel? “It is allowable, friend. “Venerable sir, is it allowable to drink water from a hollowed-out onyx vessel?
